match.reason: The bank point is a Year 12 treatment built around the three pillars of environment, economy and society, which goes beyond the simpler Year 7 brief about environments supporting people and other living things, so it is not the same depth or framing.

draft.title: Sustainability
card: Sustainability means using an environment in a way that lets it keep supporting people and other living things in the future.
If people use something faster than nature can replace it, it may run short. Over-fishing a bay is one example.
Sustainable use takes care of the environment now so that people later can still use it. This can mean taking less or using it more carefully.
A sustainable choice looks at the future as well as today's needs.
draft.remember: Sustainable use looks after an environment so it can keep supporting life.

a.q: Which choice is the most sustainable way to use a bay where people fish?
opts: Limit the catch so fish numbers can recover
Catch as many fish as possible this year
Fish only the biggest bay and ignore small ones
Stop everyone from ever using the bay
a.why: Limiting the catch lets fish numbers recover, so the bay can keep supporting people and fish. Catching as many as possible uses the fish faster than they are replaced, which is not sustainable.
a.clue: Which choice lets the fish keep being there later?

b.q: A council in Tasmania lets a company cut down a forest faster than trees regrow. Why is this not sustainable?
opts: The forest may run out and stop supporting life
The company earns money from the forest today
Cutting trees changes how the forest looks now
The forest is far from the nearest town
b.why: Trees are used faster than they regrow, so the forest may run out and no longer support people or animals. Earning money today does not show sustainability, since it ignores the future.
b.clue: Compare how fast trees are cut with how fast they regrow.

a.best: Limit the catch so fish numbers can recover

b.best: The forest may run out and stop supporting life

problems.detail: The option 'Fish only the biggest bay and ignore small ones' does not make sense, because the question is about one bay. It reads as a garbled distractor that may confuse students. Reword it, for example 'Catch only the biggest fish and throw back none'.

a.q: Which choice is the most sustainable way to use a bay where people fish?
opts: Limit the catch so fish numbers can recover
Catch as many fish as possible this year
Use bigger nets so each trip catches more fish
Stop everyone from ever using the bay
a.why: Limiting the catch lets fish numbers recover, so the bay can keep supporting people and fish. Catching as many as possible, or using bigger nets, takes fish faster than they are replaced. Stopping all use means people later cannot use the bay either.
